title: Explore What An Arts Organisation Does
objective: Explore an arts organisation through a real activity and show what its work helps people do.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Trinity Arts Award Explore. Explore What An Arts Organisation Does.
Objective: Explore an arts organisation through a real session and show what its work helps people do.
Success evidence: The real arts group’s identity, the pupil’s active exploration of its work, a finding and an exact record location. Preparation is labelled separately.
You can explore through looking, listening, asking and trying. Choose a way to take part that works for you. You do not need to share private facts about your life.
We may go to them, they may come in, or we may meet live on screen. The route comes from the current slot card. No meeting is promised by this deck.
40-minute lesson frame. Staff may extend or split the real experience across sessions.

This deck serves Explore Part B, Explore. Part B requires at least one artist AND at least one arts organisation, through live or active experience. Desk research alone fails; archives and prerecorded video are preparation only. Explore has four parts, each a distinct activity. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The whole Explore portfolio has a 10-file cap, organised digitally by part. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. Neither local training nor validation is asserted as confirmed here. Advisers must not write plans, reviews or evidence for pupils. Scribe or record the pupil's own words and check them back unchanged. Core, Extend and Challenge are support routes within Explore and retain the live or active requirement. An evidence locator names the filename plus page, slide or timecode. Read the current PRACTITIONER_SLOT and ORG_SLOT from tools/artsaward/SLOTS.json; no candidate name or date is embedded here. R1 pupils visit, R2 the artist or arts organisation comes in, R3 live remote exchange: all remain unconfirmed until actually arranged. Do not treat a recorded video as a live exchange. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. This is the organisation-focused Part B deck. Use ORG_SLOT for the actual arts organisation and check PRACTITIONER_SLOT for the separate artist element. An organisation is not evidenced by a logo or a website name alone. The pupil needs live or active exploration of its arts work, such as participation in a real group-led workshop or a guided exchange that allows a response. Do not treat a self-guided worksheet based only on a website or recorded video as that experience. A genuine encounter may also serve the artist element, but identify each role and the pupil’s exploration separately. Lab and independent time support real activity when arranged; extend or split the frame as needed. With no actual activity ready, teach the classroom model as rehearsal and retain a clear missing-experience action.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Read both current slots and identify whether a real organisation activity is ready. Do not infer a confirmed group identity from a logo or an artist’s name.

blocks.text: A group can help art happen
Find your question for the arts group. What did you want to learn about its work?
Read the current arts group card with staff. It comes from the organisation slot. If the name or session is still open, keep it open on your sheet.
An arts group may help people make art, see art or learn about art. It can work in a building, outside or through a live link.
A logo tells you a name. It does not tell you all the work that group does.
Today you will look for that work in a real session, if one is ready. If not, the classroom practice stays preparation.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Make the two simple pictures live, using scrap paper. Keep the model practical and clearly labelled rehearsal rather than claimed organisation contact.

blocks.text: Rehearsal: making space for art
The adult draws two small paper pictures. They place one flat behind a pile of books and one where everyone can see.
Which can you explore from your seat? Point to what helps or gets in the way.
Now the adult moves the hidden picture into view. The art itself has not changed. The way people can reach it has.
Showing work is one way an arts group can help. It may also provide tools, run a workshop or help people talk about art.
This is a classroom model. It gives us ideas to test against what a real group actually does.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: The display is a rehearsal of linking role to purpose, not a fake organisation case study. In the actual experience, support an action or question tied to the group’s own work.

blocks.text: Rehearsal model: a job and its purpose
Watch the adult set up a tiny paper display. First they put both pictures close together, with one covering the other.
They try to look at each picture. Then they move them apart and check the view again.
The job was to place the work. The purpose was to help people see it. Those two things link.
The adult asks, 'What changed for the person looking?' You may answer by pointing to the space they made.
Use that same link in the real arts group session. Notice a job that the group does. Ask how that job helps people make, see or learn about art.
You might be offered a workshop task, a guided look at work or a live question exchange. Take your part in the real session.
Do not assume the group runs every kind of art or does every job. Find out from the people and work involved.
If you can, check a finding in a second way. A reply and a visible action may help explain each other.
Keep the finding about this real group. A general fact about galleries is not the same thing.

blocks.title: A group role has a purpose
blocks.caption: Notice a job, ask, take part and connect.
blocks.alt: Four boxes link noticing a group job, asking its purpose, taking part in the real session and connecting the job with what it helps people do.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Suggested matches: A to 2, B to 3, C to 1. Discuss other reasonable links. These visible cards are generic rehearsal prompts, not claims about the slot organisation.

blocks.text: Visible cards: match the job and purpose
Match each job card to a purpose card. Use the words below, not a guessed story about the eventual group.
Could a job help in more than one way? Point to your best match and explain what makes it useful.
Keep these as possible roles. The real group may do different work. Find out through the experience.

items: A · Arrange pictures with space between them.
B · Set out safe tools for a workshop.
C · Invite questions about a piece of art.
1 · Help people think and talk about the work.
2 · Help people see each piece clearly.
3 · Help people try a way to make art.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Help distinguish the organisation’s role, the artist’s role and the pupil’s action. Note actual source and date after the activity. Keep any website-only work as preparation.

blocks.text: A name is a start, not the whole record
A group name tells someone which group you explored. Add what you actively found out about its work.
After the real session, name a job or action you saw. Say how you took part and what that helped you notice.
You may have used tools in a group-run workshop. You may have asked about the way work was shown. Use what actually happened.
Keep the source of a finding clear. Was it a reply from the group, something you tried, or a detail you explored with them?
A web page can help you get ready. Label that reading preparation. It does not replace the live or active element.
If an artist also took part, check their role. One experience may help you explore both. Keep a clear record for each.
Ask staff to check names and spelling. Do not fill a missing fact with a guess.

boxes.head: ARTIST
boxes.line1: the maker and their arts work
boxes.line2: what I explored about the person

boxes.head: ARTS GROUP
boxes.line1: the group and what it helps do
boxes.line2: what I actively explored with it

blocks.title: Two roles need clear evidence
blocks.caption: One real experience may help explore both roles.
blocks.alt: Two panels distinguish the artist and their work from the arts group and its role. Each needs a clear record even when explored in the same real experience.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Select the branch explicitly and allow sufficient real activity time. The classroom display remains rehearsal if no organisation experience is available.

blocks.text: Explore the real group when ready
Staff will tell you whether a real session is ready. If it is, take part through the agreed route.
Use your question to explore a job the group does. Look, listen, try or respond in a way that fits the real session.
Ask for a clearer view or a pause if you need it. Let staff help with access or tools.
If nothing is arranged yet, return to the paper display. Change the space or angle and test who can see the work.
Use that practice to improve your group question. Label it preparation. Leave the real group finding open until you have one.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Preserve the pupil’s own finding and the actual live/active action across all tiers. The organisation identity and evidence cannot be replaced by a generic description.

blocks.text: Keep your group finding
After the real session, put the group name on your record. Use the checked name from the source.
Show what you did and what you found about the group's work. Link a role to what it helps people do.
You could use a sample or short note. An agreed clip or staff account of your action may also help. Your own finding can be spoken or shown.
If the work is only preparation, keep that label. Save the useful question and tell staff which real element is still to do.
Check the artist record too. Do not mark it complete just because the group record has a name.
Save the work in Part B. Name the filename and page, slide or timecode.

items: Core · use picture or word prompts in the real arts group session. Take part with support and show what the group helped people do. Keep its real name, your own action and the file location. Label practice as preparation.
Extend · take part in the same real session and make your own record. Link a group role to something you saw or did. Keep that finding distinct from the artist’s work.
Challenge · keep the same real experience and record. Follow up a group role you found interesting. If the real session allows, ask about a change. Test how it could help people use or see the art.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: Confirm the actual status of each element. Keep unresolved names, experience or access arrangements visible as next actions, not a completed Part B claim.

blocks.text: Find the role in your record
Point to the part of your record that shows the group's work. Say what it helped you or other people do.
Ask an adult to find the same part using your location note. Fix the note if needed.
Check whether both the artist and the group have real experience records now. Any missing element stays a next action.
Keep a question you still want to explore. Next time you will use the records to connect the two roles. Add no facts that are not there.

print.intro: Explore a real arts organisation through a live or active experience when arranged. Record its name, your own action and what you found about its work. Classroom practice stays preparation.
focusRows: Which real group did I explore, and how do I know its name?
What did I actively do with the group?
What role did I find, and what did it help people do?
Are the group and artist separately evidenced, and where are the records?
tiers: Core · use picture or word prompts in the real arts group session. Take part with support and show what the group helped people do. Keep its real name, your own action and the file location. Label practice as preparation.
Extend · take part in the same real session and make your own record. Link a group role to something you saw or did. Keep that finding distinct from the artist’s work.
Challenge · keep the same real experience and record. Follow up a group role you found interesting. If the real session allows, ask about a change. Test how it could help people use or see the art.
checks: The arts organisation is real and its name comes from the checked source.
The record shows live or active work, or is honestly labelled preparation.
My own action and finding about the group’s arts work are clear.
The artist element is checked separately, even if one experience served both.
Each record names a filename plus page, slide or timecode.
